tools.name: maps_search
tools.description:
Search Google Maps for locations.

This tool utilizes a subagent that uses the Google Maps API as a tool to search for locations following the provided query prompt.
Example use cases:
- Place-specific questions: "Is there a cafe near the corner of 1st and Main that has outdoor seating?"
- Finding the best locations by reviews: "Which family-friendly restaurants near here have the best playground reviews?"
- Itinerary planning: "Plan a day in San Francisco for me. I want to see the Golden Gate Bridge, visit a museum, and have a nice dinner."

Args:
    query: Natural language prompt describing what to find on Google Maps.

query.description: Natural language prompt describing what to find on Google Maps.

tools.name: update_space_settings
tools.description:
Update space settings — either globally or for a single page route.

By default (`path=""`) the call updates space-wide settings stored in
`site-settings.json`. Pass a route path (e.g. `path="/"` for the home page
or `path="/about"`) to apply the change as a per-page override that
inherits from the space defaults when unset.

Only provided arguments are changed; omitted arguments keep their current
values. Pass "default" for any string field to clear it (revert to the
space default when path is set, revert to the built-in default when path
is empty). Triggers a zo-space server restart so changes take effect
immediately.

Per-page overrides only support `site_title`, `site_description`,
`og_image_url`, and `noindex` — they map onto `page_title`,
`page_description`, `page_og_image_url`, and `page_noindex` ("block" /
"allow"). The other fields apply space-globally only and will be
rejected if combined with a non-empty `path`.

Args:
    path: Empty string for space-global settings (default), or a route
        path like "/" (home) or "/about" to update that page's metadata
        overrides. Note: "" is the global sentinel and is distinct from
        "/" which is the home route.
    site_title: Title override. Pass "default" to reset/clear.
    site_description: Meta description. Pass "default" to reset/clear.
    og_image_url: Asset path for OG image (e.g. "/assets/og.png"). Must
        be a space asset, not an external URL. Pass "default" to revert.
    favicon_url: Asset path for favicon. Space-global only.
    custom_head_html: HTML injected into <head>. Space-global only.
    robots_txt: Custom robots.txt content. Space-global only.
    noindex: "true" adds noindex/nofollow; "false" removes it; "default"
        clears any per-page override (and inherits from the space).
    custom_404_route: Route path for custom 404 page. Space-global only.
    lang: HTML lang attribute value. Space-global only.
    atproto_did: AT Protocol DID for domain verification. Space-global only.

tools.name: edit_persona
tools.description:
Edit an existing persona — heavily biased toward additive, surgical changes.

There is no full-replacement option here on purpose: a persona is the user's identity for the agent, and wholesale rewrites are almost always the wrong move. To create a brand-new persona, use create_persona instead.

Prompt changes go through prompt_edit, which is merged into the existing prompt via an LLM. Use '// ... existing content ...' to leave large unchanged sections untouched. Almost all edits should be additive — appending a bullet, recording an observed preference, refining tone — rather than rewording or removing existing content. Never delete or shorten the prompt unless the user has explicitly asked you to.

Args:
    persona_id: Identifier of the persona to update.
    name: New display name, if renaming.
    prompt_edit: Edit to apply to the prompt. Provide only the changed sections, with '// ... existing content ...' placeholders for unchanged parts. Merged into the existing prompt via LLM. Strongly prefer additive edits.
    edit_instructions: One short sentence describing what the edit does. Used with prompt_edit.
    image: New image URL for the avatar.
    image_hue: New HSL hue angle (0-360 integer) tinting the chrome Pegasus avatar. Anchors: 0=red, 60=yellow, 120=green, 180=cyan, 240=blue, 300=magenta (wraps at 360). Pass -1 to leave unchanged.
    model: AI model ID for the persona, if updating.

persona_id.description: Identifier of the persona to update.

prompt_edit.description: Edit to apply to the prompt. Provide only the changed sections, with '// ... existing content ...' placeholders for unchanged parts. Merged into the existing prompt via LLM. Strongly prefer additive edits.

tools.name: search_app_catalog
tools.description:
Search Pipedream's full catalog of 1000+ app integrations by keyword.

Use this to find an integration that does NOT have a dedicated `use_app_*`
tool. Returns matching apps with their `app_slug`, name, and description,
plus whether the workspace has already connected each one.

Catalog apps are beyond Zo's curated, verified set — they work, but Zo has
not tested them, so reliability varies. When a dedicated `use_app_*` tool
exists for what the user wants, prefer that.

Once you've found an app:
  1. `connect_integration(app_slug)` — if it isn't connected yet.
  2. `list_app_tools(app_slug)` — see its actions and parameters.
  3. `use_integration(app_slug, tool_name, configured_props={...})`.

Create a new route or fully rewrite an existing one in the user's zo.space site.

See <capabilities> for architecture details, examples, and styling guidance.

IMPORTANT: For edits to an existing route, use `edit_space_route` instead — it sends only the changed sections and avoids re-transmitting the whole file. Only use `write_space_route` when creating a new route or intentionally replacing all of the existing code.

tools.name: connect_integration
tools.description:
Surface an inline Connect button so the user can authorize an OAuth integration.

USE THIS whenever the user asks to do something with an OAuth integration
that is NOT yet connected for this workspace.  Five flavours, same
user-facing card:

- Pipedream apps: ``gmail``, ``notion``, ``google_calendar``,
  ``google_tasks``, ``google_drive``, ``linear``, ``dropbox``,
  ``spotify``, ``google_sheets``, ``airtable_oauth``,
  ``microsoft_onedrive``, ``microsoft_outlook``.
- X (Twitter): pass ``app_slug="x"``.
- GitHub: pass ``app_slug="github"``. Opens a ``gh auth login``
  device-code dialog inline. Use this when the user wants GitHub
  access (PRs, repos, issues) and the workspace's gh CLI isn't
  authenticated yet — readiness is whether ``gh auth status`` passes.
- Stripe Connect: pass ``app_slug="stripe"``. Use this when the user
  wants to accept payments / sell products with Stripe and Stripe
  Connect isn't set up yet. The widget sends them to Settings →
  Integrations → Payments to finish onboarding (it does not run an
  inline OAuth flow). This is Zo's native Stripe integration — do NOT
  try to connect Stripe through the generic Pipedream catalog.
- OAuth MCP servers: pass ``app_slug="mcp:<slug>"`` — ``mcp:logfire``,
  ``mcp:sentry``, ``mcp:linear``, ``mcp:notion``, ``mcp:posthog``,
  ``mcp:cloudflare``, ``mcp:ahrefs``.
- Any other Pipedream catalog app: pass the ``app_slug`` from
  ``search_app_catalog`` results. The full 1000+ app catalog is
  connectable this way — not just the curated apps listed above.

The ``mcp:`` prefix disambiguates MCP servers from Pipedream apps —
notably ``linear`` (Pipedream) is distinct from ``mcp:linear`` (the
Linear MCP server), and likewise ``notion`` vs ``mcp:notion``.

Prefer this over telling the user to navigate to Settings — the inline
widget is one click vs. several, and looks better.

The widget renders inline in chat.  When the user clicks Connect and
completes the OAuth round-trip, the connection is finalized automatically
and the widget flips to "Connected" — you do NOT need to wait for a tool
result or take any further action.  Your turn ends after you surface the
widget; connecting does NOT wake you back up.  Only on the user's *next
message* will your capabilities reflect the new connection state, at which
point you can proceed with the original request.

After calling this tool, briefly acknowledge in chat that you've surfaced
a Connect button (one short sentence is enough — the widget speaks for
itself), and ask the user to let you know once they've connected so you
can continue.  Do NOT say or imply that clicking Connect will make you
automatically pick up where you left off ("once you connect, I'll
generate…") — that is misleading, because you stay idle until the user
sends another message.  Do not also link to Settings; the widget already
exposes that as an alternative.

Do NOT call this tool if the app is already connected (check the
<capabilities> block) — that just clutters the chat with a redundant
card.  Do NOT call multiple times for the same `app_slug` in one turn.

Note: ``linear`` / ``notion`` (Pipedream) and ``mcp:linear`` /
``mcp:notion`` (MCP servers) are distinct integrations.  Use whichever
matches what the user asked for — if they're in MCP code mode or asked
for "the Linear MCP", use ``mcp:linear``; otherwise the Pipedream
``linear`` is usually what they want.

Do NOT use this for chat channels (Telegram, Discord) or AI model
providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, ...): Zo supports those natively — link the
user to the relevant settings page instead (Settings -> Channels or
Settings -> AI -> Providers).
